title: Machining of standard mechanical parts
description: Division: DOE. Call for Tender (CFT) covering build-to-print manufacturing and machining of mechanical parts. The CFT is scheduled to be issued in Q4/2022 to companies in the ESO Member States. The scope of work includes manufacturing and machining of mechanical parts according to ESO 2D drawings, 3D CAD data and ESO specifications, and their agreed upon on-time delivery to ESO Headquarters in Garching (near Munich), Germany. The contractor(s) shall be capable to provide standard and precision machining processes such as milling (3-axis and 5-axis), turning and cutting to be applied on typical construction materials such as aluminium alloys, steel, stainless steel, copper, brass, plastics and epoxies. Special materials such as Invar, Molybdenum (TZM) and ceramics are not excluded. Main requirements on contractor(s) (minimum): · CAD/CAM systems; · ISO 9001:2015 certified; · 15 machines 3-axis CNC-milling; · 7 machines 5-axis CNC-milling; · 15 machines CNC-turning; · 1 Flat grinding machine; and · Stock of raw materials. The multiple suppliers frame contracts are expected to be awarded in Q4/2022, for a firm period of three years (frame contracts start date Q1/2023), to two Bidders, which have submitted fully compliant Tenders and offer the lowest prices. title: Design, production, installation and commissioning of the ELT Liquid Nitrogen infrastructure
description: Division: DOP/ELT. Preliminary Inquiry (PI) to identify and select companies that are interested in and capable of manufacturing the Liquid Nitrogen (LIN) infrastructure for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) and installing it at ELT site in northern Chile, at ca. 3,000 meters above sea level. The PI will be released in Q3/2022 to potential suppliers in the ESO Member States and Chile and will be followed by a Call for tender planned to be issued in Q4/2022. The scope of work includes system design, manufacture, verification testing and transportation to the ELT site in Chile. It also includes installation and acceptance testing at the ELT Observatory in collaboration with ESO, anticipated to take place in the first half of 2026. The LIN infrastructure system is spread over various locations inside of the multi-storey ELT building. It is an automated closed circuit distribution system, composed of cryogenic industry standards such as pressurized LIN phase-separators and storage tanks (3000-4000 L volume), several hundred metres of vacuum-insulated interconnection piping (size DN 20-63), automatic LIN supply and level control, Nitrogen gas exhaust system with gas heaters, cryogenic valves and safety installations. The contract is expected to be awarded in Q2/2023 to the Bidder which has submitted a fully compliant Tender and offers the best value for money for ESO, taking into account the quality and price of the offer. description: Division: DOO. Preliminary Inquiry followed by a Call for Tender: Preliminary Inquiry (PI) to identify and select companies that are interested in and capable of providing software development services for the development of front-end and back-end scientific operation dataflow software for the ESO observatories. The PI will be released in Q4/2022 to potential suppliers in the ESO Member States and will be followed by a Call for tender planned to be issued at the end of Q4/2022. The Call for Tender (CfT) will cover software development and testing services of operational dataflow software applications for ESO VLT/ELT/ALMA Observatories. Service Contract: The contract will start on 1 January 2024 (with a phase-in period as of 2023 Q4), for a firm period of 3 years, with the option to extend it by up to 2 more years. The CFT is scheduled to be issued in Q4/2022 to companies in the ESO Member States. Scope: The scope of work includes the development of front-end and back-end scientific operation dataflow software for the ESO observatories. It covers design, implementation, and testing of operational dataflow software applications for ESO VLT/ELT/ALMA Observatories. The contract will be structured around clearly defined deliverables using an agile process with roughly one to two months iteration cycles. At the end of each cycle the product for the next cycle will be agreed. The technical focus of this contract is on developing and testing REST and GraphQL APIs in Java with a database backend (both SQL and noSQL) and web interfaces in Angular/TypeScript. The contractor should have as a minimum the following experience/capabilities: · Proven professional experience developing software in Java. · Proven experience interfacing Java to relational databases (JDBC, JPA, Spring). · Proven experience developing Java web applications. · Proven experience with software architecture and API specification · Proven experience with RESTful and GraphQL API development. · Proven experience with test automation of APIs and web user interfaces. · Proven experience with Angular JS. · Familiarity with Agile software development process. · Solid practical familiarity with modern software engineering practices and tools, including configuration control tools, incremental & iterative development, unit and integration testing and the Linux environment. · Experience in the development and maintenance of software products in the science domain will be an asset. · The company shall use the development infrastructure to be provided by ESO (for version control, issue management, etc..). · The software shall be developed in a continuous integration system provided by ESO, building a running demonstration of the application. The contract is expected to be awarded in Q2/2023, to the Bidder, which has submitted a fully compliant Tender and offers the best value for money for ESO taking into account the quality and price of the offer. title: Next generation laser frequency comb calibration system for ESO’s high resolution spectrographs
description: Division: DOE (ELT). The project aims at the research and development of a next generation calibration system for ESO’s high resolution spectrographs. The goal is the development of a reliable, turn-key calibration system, which covers the optical and NIR spectral range (0.37-1.8 µm) offered by ESO’s instruments with (tens of) thousands of unresolved spectral lines. The wavelengths of the individual calibration lines should be known from first principles to an accuracy equal or better than 1cm/s. The immediate objectives of the project are to determine the most promising technology and technical implementation of such a calibration system, based on one or two design studies and to increase the technical readiness through prototyping where necessary. The long-term goal is the development, production and delivery of the system. The contract covering this latter phase may be placed without further competition. According to the current plan, the design studies should start in Q4 2022. The initial design studies should take approx. 12 months, starting right after the contract award. The goal is to kick-off the development/production contract about one year after concluding the study contracts. ESO intends to release a RFI in Q1/Q2 2022. Scheduled/Status:

The goal is the development of a reliable, turn-key calibration system, which covers the optical and NIR spectral range (0.37-1.8 µm) offered by ESO’s instruments with (tens of) thousands of unresolved spectral lines. The wavelengths of the individual calibration lines should be known from first principles to an accuracy equal or better than 1cm/s. The immediate objectives of the project are to determine the most promising technology and technical implementation of such a calibration system, based on one or two design studies and to increase the technical readiness through prototyping where necessary. The long-term goal is the development, production and delivery of the system. The contract covering this latter phase may be placed without further competition. According to the current plan, the design studies should start in Q4 2022. The initial design studies should take approx. 12 months, starting right after the contract award. The goal is to kick-off the development/production contract about one year after concluding the study contracts. ESO intends to release a RFI in Q1/Q2 2022. Scheduled/Status:

title: Price inquiry (PQ) for the production of six pyramid prisms. The scope of work includes the manufacturing, polishing, coating, and testing of 6 special prisms made out of the low dispersion glass S-FPL55. The prisms shall have a dimension of approximately 30 mm diameter and a height of 10 mm. The prims shall have a pyramid shape on one side, i. e. four facets converging in a tip under a shallow angle of approx. 4 degrees. The pyramid edge and tip shall be sharp with a thickness of 10 micron or less within the central few millimetres around the tip of the prism. The prism backside shall be flat. title: Service Contract for the Development of ELT Control System Software
description: Division: DOP. Call for tender (CFT) procuring software development services for the development of control software for ESO’s Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) which is currently under construction. The ELT control system is a distributed system of Linux servers connected over Ethernet. The service contract shall contribute to existing in-house software projects developing various components of the ELT control software. The applications are typically multi-threaded C++ applications on Linux, with Python/Qt and Python user interfaces. Development will be carried out following an agile process with one-month iterations. The company shall use the development infrastructure and tools provided by ESO. Mandatory skills for the service company: · Proven professional experience developing software in C++/Linux and Python; · Solid practical familiarity with modern software engineering practices and tools, including configuration control tools (git), debuggers and profilers, incremental & iterative development, unit and integration testing on Linux; · Good command of the English language, both oral and written; · Experience with DDS, ZeroMQ and multicast UDP beneficial; and · Experience with OPC and TwinCAT for Beckhoff PLCs beneficial. The work shall be carried out primarily at the contractor premises, accessing ESO development infrastructure remotely. Occasional onsite visits to ESO (Garching) may be required. The Call for tender is scheduled to be issued in Q4/2022 to potential suppliers in the ESO Member States and Chile. The service contract shall have an adaptable Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) envelope of around four FTEs per year. The service will cover an initial duration of two years and includes an option for extension on a year by year basis, up to a further three years (i.e. a maximum duration of five years). The contract is expected to be awarded in Q1/2023 to the bidder, which has submitted a fully compliant tender and offers the best value for money for ESO considering the quality and price of the offer. description: Division: DOO. Request for information (RFI) to investigate the solutions available and to identify companies that are interested in and capable of providing optical based dedicated communication channels of at least 100Gbps bandwidth, to connect the Paranal Observatory located 120km south of Antofagasta, in the Atacama region, and the ESO offices in Vitacura, Santiago RM. After the RFI results the following procurement strategy and plan were established: Preliminary Inquiry (PI) to identify and select companies that are interested in and capable of providing optical based dedicated communication channels of at least 40Gbps bandwidth, to connect the Paranal Observatory located 120km south of Antofagasta with the ESO offices in Vitacura, Santiago de Chile. The PI will be released in Q3/2022 to potential suppliers in Chile and will be followed by a Call for tender planned to be issued in Q4/2022. The scope of work includes the optical based dedicated communication channels of at least 40Gbps bandwidth, the provision of DWDM equipment, the maintenance and operation of the infrastructure. title: Technology Solutions for the ESO Paranal Observatory Integrated Operations
description: Division: LPO. Request for information (RFI) to investigate different solutions available on the market for the implementation of the Integrated Operations processes for the ESO Observatories at Paranal. The RFI will be released within Q1/2022 to potential suppliers in the ESO Member States, Chile and Australia. The RFI foresees the organisation of one or more Industry Day/s for the exchange of information between ESO and interested suppliers. The exact dates and number of Industry Days will be communicated to interested suppliers during the RFI. title: Retrofit of the Large Integration Hall at the ESO HQ.
description: Division: 06.05.2021. In order to test sensitive instruments in the Large Integration Hall (LIH, size: L 21.5 x W 16.2 x H 13.7m) of the Technical Building (construction from 2014) at ESO premises in Garching the existing HVAC-installations need to be re-designed. Therefore it needs to be checked if existing components need to be retrofitted or complemented or – more likely – a completely new HVAC-system needs to be installed after removing the old equipment. Involved trades are HVAC, electrical works and measurement, control and regulation technology. Ventilation and refrigeration technology have to be changed in a way that pre-defined room conditions can be achieved at all times during the year. (temperature and humidity, air flow, cleanliness aspects have to be considered as well) Additional process cooling for cooling instruments also has to be provided in the same course. Several smaller works such as a new ventilation system in the basement and an exhaust extraction system in a workshop also have to be realized. The project is divided into two parts: 1. the complete planning work, including cost-calculations, a detailed planning and construction management including the support during the complete warranty period 2. the whole construction works, consisting works on HVAC-system, electrical works and management and control system that will remain in place and only has to be complemented. Two possible models regarding the construction works are considered: 2.1. General Contractor including all three trades as well as smaller structural works 2.2. Several single contracts, where HVAC will be the major one. The PI/CFT for the planning work will be released in Q2/2021 to potential suppliers in the ESO Member States and will be followed by a CFT for the construction planned to be issued in Q4/2021. The project will be awarded to Bidders, which have submitted a fully compliant Tender and offer the best value for money for ESO taking into account the quality and price of the offer. description: Division: ALMA. Request for information (RFI) to identify companies that are interested in and capable of providing communication services for the ALMA sites. The Service Contract shall start on 01.02.2022 after the proper installation and testing period (1 month – starting 01.01.2022) of the required components and shall consider a firm period of 3 years with the option to extend it for 2 more years. title: Design and construction of the access road to the CTA South site
description: Division: CTA. A Preliminary Inquiry (PI) will be issued in Q1/2021 to identify the companies that have interest and capabilities to perform the design and construction of approximately 3 Kms of asphalt paved road from the future junction with the public road B710 to the CTA-South site, located at the Paranal Observatory, 130 kms south of Antofagasta, Atacama Region. The subsequent Call for Tender is planned for Q2/2021. The scope of work will cover the following tasks: - identify the most appropriate trajectory of the road, from an economical and safety perspective mainly; - perform topography and geotechnical analysis (test pits and laboratory material analysis); - develop basic and detailed design of the road following the Chilean Standard Manual de Carreteras; - construct the road according to the previously approved design. The structure of the road shall be calculated according to standard load profiles, and is most likely expected to be done of stone layers with an asphalt top cover (cap seal). The Contractor shall be enrolled in the list of companies approved by the Chilean Road authority (Vialidad, a department of the Ministerio de Obras Publicas). The contract is expected to be awarded in Q4/2021 to the Bidder, which has submitted a fully compliant Tender and offers the best value for money for ESO taking into account the quality and price of the offer. description: Division: DOE (ELT). The project aims for the development of dispersive photonic chips (e.g. arrayed waveguide gratings) working at near infrared wavelengths. Depending on the technical feasibility the chips shall work in the bands (J-band) 1.1-1.3 µm and (K-band) 2.05-2.45 µm. description: Division: DOE/DOO. The scope of this Call for Tender is to outsource software testing services for the VLT/ELT/ALMA dataflow software. Specifically, the scope of the work is for dataflow applications related to Program Preparation, Program Selection, Observation Preparation, Operations Support and Science Archive. The contract will be structured around defined testing services using an agile process with roughly one to two months iteration cycles. The technical focus of this service contract is on testing Java and web-based applications for the VLT/ELT and ALMA dataflow systems. title: Design, Manufacture, and Certification of the ERIS System Handling Tool
description: Division: DOE. The scope of this Price Inquiry is to procure the design, manufacture, assembly, and certification of a handling tool. This tool is intended to support and transport the ERIS Instrumentation System over short distances, and then lift and provide fine positioning during the integration with either the Very Large Telescope (VLT) or a telescope simulator. The handling tool will be used during initial testing in Europe and then inside the VLT enclosure at Paranal in Chile during initial integration and subsequent maintenance activities. The scope of work includes the following tasks: - The design the handling tool in accordance with the technical requirements. - The manufacture and assembly of the handling tool - To provide all necessary certification and documentation. - Delivery of the handling tool to ESO headquarters. Some very basic information regarding the handling tool is as follows: - The ERIS instrument to be handled is approximately 3 tonnes - The handling tool shall be capable of lifting the ERIS instrument by a minimum height of 600mm. - The handling tool itself shall remain with a volume measuring approximately 3184x2900x450mm when in its lowered configuration The contractor providing the services should have prior experience in the design, manufacture, and certification of specialized lifting and handling equipment. The contract shall last 6 months, the contract is expected to start in August 2018. The Price Inquiry will be issued to potential suppliers in the ESO Member States and Australia. Scheduled/Status:
